ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A square conducting wire frame with side length L starts from rest on a smooth inclined plane with inclination angle θ and slides down along the inclined plane, then enters the uniform magnetic field below the dashed line that is perpendicular to the inclined plane and upward. As shown in Figure 15, the inclined plane and the magnetic field below the dashed line extend downward far enough. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When the wire frame slides down from different heights, during the process of entering the magnetic field, the amounts of charge passing through the cross section of the wire of the frame are equal

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A square conducting wire frame with side length L starts from rest on a smooth inclined plane with inclination angle θ and slides down along the inclined plane, then enters the uniform magnetic field below the dashed line that is perpendicular to the inclined plane and upward. As shown in Figure 15, the inclined plane and the magnetic field below the dashed line extend downward far enough. When the wire frame slides down from different heights, during the process of entering the magnetic field, what is the relationship between the amounts of charge passing through the cross section of the wire of the frame?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a section of an inclined plane, with the inclination angle θ marked at the bottom; there is a dashed boundary line on the inclined plane, and in the region below the dashed line several arrows are drawn and labeled B, indicating that there is a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the inclined plane in this region; above the dashed line there is a square conducting wire frame, which, after sliding down along the inclined plane, will enter the magnetic-field region below the dashed line from the region without magnetic field. Reasoning: The side length of the wire frame is L, and let the total resistance of the wire frame be R. Releasing from different heights will only change the speed of the wire frame when it reaches the magnetic-field boundary, thereby changing the time of the entering process and the magnitude of the instantaneous induced current. During the process of entering the magnetic field, the total amount of charge passing through a certain wire cross section is q=∫I dt. From Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, I=ε/R, and ε=|dΦ/dt|, so q=(1/R)∫|dΦ/dt|dt. During the process in which the wire frame enters the magnetic field, the magnetic flux monotonically increases from 0 to B L^2, therefore q=|Φ末-Φ初|/R=B L^2/R. This result does not contain the release height or entering speed, so when sliding down from different heights, during the process of the wire frame entering the magnetic field, the amounts of charge passing through the wire cross section are equal.
